sections.html: Maximum total length about 20 cm. Carnivorous. Origin: Venezuela.
• IUCN Red List: Least Concern (IUCN 2023). The species is widely distributed and faces no direct threats.

Three different species of the genus Tetranematichthys are currently distinguished by scientists. None of them is often imported, because their secretive way of life between dead driftwood makes catching them a pure matter of luck. This is the first importation ever of Tetranematichthys wallacei, from Venezuela. Three specimens were obtained: one male and two females.
South America: Amazon basin: upper Negro River system in Brazil and Venezuela and upper Orinoco River basin in southern Venezuela.
A tank for Tetranematichthys should contain fine sand on the bottom, be softly lit and be equipped with a great number of pieces of driftwood.

It is carnivorous and prefers to feed on small fish. Prefers live foods given at lights out. Try different choices of frozen foods to see what they prefer as they can be picky in their dietary requirements.
During the daytime the fish often sleep lying on their side. This behaviour is absolutely normal and no reason for concern. Towards conspecifics Tetranematichthys are completely peaceful.
The males develop an extended dorsal fin and is thorny.

As in the closely related genus Ageinosus, males of Tetranematichthys develop enormous dorsal fins during the breeding season. The spine of that fin is very thorny. During mating the males attach to the female with this thorny spine. Fertilisation is internal, by a penis-like organ formed from modified rays of the anal fin. It is said that after the breeding season the male's dorsal fin reduces to the size of the female's.
Tetranematichthys means "fish with four threads", referring to the barbels. wallacei is a dedication name for Alfred Russel Wallace (1823-1913).

Description: Distinguished from T. quadrifilis in the alignment of the lateral margins of the head in the region from the anterior margin of the orbit to the posterior limit of the opercle (running approximately in parallel from ventral view vs. diverging laterally, respectively); in the body width at the pectoral-fin insertion as a proportion of the head width at the posterior margin of the orbit (0.99-1.10 vs. 1.17-1.25, respectively); in the distance from the tip of the snout to the anal fin origin (0.29-0.32 of SL vs. 0.33-0.36 of SL, respectively); and in the position of the anterior termination of the gill opening (one orbital diameter posterior of the transverse plane running through the posterior margin of the orbit vs. positioned in the transverse plane running through the center of the orbit, respectively).

Etymology: The genus name Tetranematichthys means "fish with four threats"; this refers to the barbels. The specific name wallacei: named after Alfred Russel Wallace when, starting in 1848, made large collections of plants and animals in the Amazon basin.
